In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiology of exercise-induced anaphyla-xis and food-dependent exercise-induced anaphy-laxis,
the development of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of exercise-induced anaphlyaxis and food-dependent exercise-induced anaphyaxis.
the pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, and treatment of EIA and its variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EIA and FDI are rare but potentially fatal conditions.
the pathogenesis and treatment of EIA and, particularly, FDEIA are still not fully understood.
exercise and food-induced anaphylactic syndromes are not fully understood and require more research to elucidate the pathophysiology and to improve the diagnosis and treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise-induced anaphyaxis (EIA), food-dependent exercise-induced anaphlyaxis (FDEI) are rare but life-threatening clinical syndomes.
the diagnosis and management of EIA and food-dependent exercise-induced anaphyla-xis are not well established and require further studies.
the diagnosis of EIA and/or FDEIA is based on a careful history and a thorough physical examination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EIA/FDEIA should be suspected when a person experiences anaphylaxis only during exercise.
the diagnosis is based on a careful anamnesis, and treatment is focused on avoidance of triggering food and exercise, as well as on prompt administration of epinephrine in cases of acute anaphylaxis.
EIA and FEDIA are potentially life-threatening conditions that can be managed with lifestyle changes and avoidance of the offending food.
